scope: Eight unselected Books 10–16 canonical lesson drafts; seven-step content and source-owner comparison
buildCheck: Focused build and --check independently pass: 8 lessons, 48 questions, 32 audio requests, 0 structural flags.
originalityScreen: Compared 192 learner-facing English strings with all 2,604 guide examples: 9 six-word matches, all fixed-target overlaps; 0 non-target six-word matches. This is a screen, not a substitute for the editorial review below.

lessonReviews.note: Have legs asks about credible future viability after repeat demand and support; prior 2255 staying power evaluates demonstrated durability over time. All four reply options are supported, and both writing models include the first-week, month-three and next-term facts.

Catch fire assesses a rapid burst of diffusion; selected 3914 catch on covers becoming adopted without itself requiring this abrupt burst. Source and examples have matching target forms, and long-term survival is not inferred.
The core academic-burden sense and seven decisions are sound, but writing model 2 omits the required priority-setting support; see R3933-01.
The stress-relief claim remains temporary and does not erase the forthcoming task; four replies and both changed-context models are grounded.

Build character teaches developing positive qualities through a specific responsibility and reflection. Legacy 907 shape character is the broader influence-on-character concept, so the source-target and learning outcome are distinguishable.
The lesson preserves limited easing of friction without claiming agreement. Both writing models retain the warehouse-hours dispute, one week of collaboration and calmer meetings.
Advertised versus delivered facts support overhyped without erasing the positive food judgement; two writing models preserve the five/two/three count.
The excessive frequency remains an excess of an otherwise valued tour. Both models preserve the weekly-to-six-daily change, fatigue and reduction rather than cancellation.

findings.issue: The prompt and self-check require the tutor to help Lok set priorities. Model 2 says only that the tutor offered a planning meeting; the purpose of that meeting is unstated, so the model does not demonstrate the full transfer task.
findings.evidence: Prompt: 導師同意與他訂優先次序. Self-check: 導師協助訂優先次序. Model 2: 'his tutor has offered a planning meeting' / '導師於是提議開會規劃'.
findings.recommendedRepair: State explicitly in both model-2 languages that the meeting will help Lok set priorities among the reports and exam; recalculate any affected exact glossary spans and bump contentRevision.

releaseLimit: All author and independent AI reviews remain provisional. No human sign-off, manifest selection or publication is implied.
